messages:
sam: heads up — the new sample-app typechecks fine in node but fails under strict tsconfig when bundled for edge. error is about overload resolution turning everything into `any`/`unknown` in the SDK types.

_taylor: ugh that sounds familiar. which combo of tsconfig + bundler?_

sam: reproducible with `module: ES2022`, `moduleResolution: bundler` (tsc 5.2), and esbuild rollup for an edge target (Cloudflare worker). error shows up as: `TS7010: Type 'any' is not assignable to type 'T'` coming from our overloaded `request` signatures.

jin: can you paste the minimal signatures? often overload order or a generic default helps.

sam: sure — simplified:```ts
// lib/request.d.ts (simplified)
export function request(options: { model: string }): Promise<string>;
export function request<T>(options: { model: string; parse?: (s: string) => T }): Promise<T>;
export async function request(options: any) { /* impl */ }
```

sam: under strict/bundler the second overload seems to lose type inference and callers get `Promise<any>` unless they explicitly annotate T.

olivia: try flipping to a single generic with default unknown:```ts
export function request<T = unknown>(opts: { model: string; parse?: (s: string)=>T }): Promise<T>;
```

olivia: also add a narrow typed overload for the common case if you really want `Promise<string>` default. overloads can confuse the bundler/ts resolver.

jin: +1. another pattern is a discriminated response wrapper so the return type is stable:```ts
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: Error };
export function request<T = string>(opts: { model: string; parse?: (s: string)=>T }): Promise<Result<T>>;
```

sam: interesting. part of the trouble is our published package `exports` and `types` fields — node consumers pick up the cjs types but edge bundles import the ESM entry which points to a slightly different .d.ts layout. maybe that mismatch is why bundler/tsc resolve differs.

_taylor: can you show the current package.json fields?_

sam: snippet:```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
},
"types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts",
"main": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "./dist/esm/index.js"
```

sam: the `types` path points to a single d.ts that assumes the CJS build shape — switching to per-entry `typesVersions` or providing explicit `exports` with `types` subkeys seems to help.

olivia: for edge workers also watch `type: "module"` at package root; bundlers sometimes prefer the `import` entry which must have matching .d.ts exports. adding "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts", "import": ... }} fixed a similar bug for me.

jin: if we can't change consumers fast, short-term we should: 1) add a single-generic public signature (no overloads) 2) ship `.d.ts` that aligns with both bundles, or 3) set `skipLibCheck: true` in the sample app tsconfig to unblock onboarding.

sam: we already do (3) as a stopgap in the quickstart but that's a bad DX. users see weird `any` inferred in their code and blame the SDK.

ci-bot: build / sample-app / e2e failed on latest commit — tsc errors in worker build. See CI log: https://ci.redwood/123/build/456 :warning:

_taylor: filing a tiny PR to 1) replace overloads with a generic default, 2) add an esm .d.ts export, and 3) update the quickstart tsconfig with a comment about `moduleResolution` workarounds. will link PR in a bit.

olivia: also add a small test that compiles the sample app with `moduleResolution: "bundler"` + `module: "ES2022"` in CI. that should catch regressions.

sam: awesome — if anyone wants to help repro locally i can drop a minimal repo. i'd like the fix to avoid `any` hacks and prefer `unknown` or discriminated wrappers so callers are forced to handle parsing errors instead of silently getting `any`. :+1:

jin: i'll take the repro and try a few tsconfig permutations. also double-check our published rollup/esbuild pipeline doesn't strip `declarationMap` or re-emit different shapes between cjs/esm. that bite me before.

sam: thanks all. leaving this thread as the tracker for the CR. linking the CI failure once PR is up. :wave:
